title: Split-lighting scenes
summary: One half of the frame in sun, the other in shadow — the meter splits the difference and misses both.
why: Matrix metering averages the whole frame. With a hard light boundary, the average is an exposure that exists nowhere in the scene: the bright half too hot, the dark half too thin.

steps.text: Hold the metering button, spin rear dial to spot
Move the focus point onto the sunlit side
Half-press to meter, hold AE-L, recompose
Let the dark half go dark — that's the picture

pitfalls: Don't try to save both halves with +comp — the sunlit side burns first and it's unrecoverable.
levelUp: Put the boundary on a compositional line — a ridge, a wall edge — and the split becomes the subject instead of a problem.
